correctness.rationale: The pseudoperiod equation is checked only for i<n−12, and the forbidden exponent threshold includes equality. Every newly created forbidden factor must be a suffix; it has some period p and at least L_p=ceil(55p/21) letters, so checking the last L_p letters for period p is equivalent to the full new-factor condition. Both constraints are prefix-closed, hence binary extension from the empty word without pruning any valid prefix is exhaustive. A separately implemented C++ depth-first enumerator visited exactly 202253 valid prefixes through length 201, with exactly 2 at length 200 and 0 at length 201, and reproduced the source certificate count tail. The two 200-bit words are complements and individually palindromes; there cannot be a longer valid word because every 202-bit word would have a 201-bit valid prefix, which does not exist.

value.rationale: The (9,12) instance is the longest finite cutoff in the published pseudoperiod table, making classification of the extreme boundary a natural finite combinatorics-on-words problem. Exactly two complementary palindromes is a complete and surprisingly rigid equality classification; it is not an arbitrary slice or reproduction of the already-known scalar bound. A correct exhaustively certified finite fact can be mathematically useful without a general theorem for other pseudoperiods.
